senses.definition: used with **the** before an uncountable noun to mean the smallest amount, when three or more amounts are being compared
senses.explanation: **Least** is the superlative of **little**: it compares three or more amounts and picks out the smallest one. It almost always follows **the**: *the least money*, *the least effort*. For a countable noun, the matching word is **the fewest**, not **the least**.

examples.text: She has the least experience of anyone on the team.
Choose the option that costs the least money.
He put in the least effort and still passed.
Of the three routes, this one takes the least time.

compare.note: **less** compares two amounts; **least** compares three or more and picks the smallest

phrases.definition: used before a number or amount to mean not less than, and possibly more
phrases.explanation: **At least** can also mean *even if nothing else is true or good*, used to point out one good thing in a bad situation: *At least you tried*.

examples.text: It will take at least two hours to get there.
There were at least fifty people at the party.

usage_note: **Least** is the superlative determiner used with an uncountable noun, almost always after **the**; the matching superlative for a countable noun is **the fewest**, not **the least**.

learner_errors.note: **Least** goes with an uncountable amount; the matching word for a countable noun is **fewest**.

learner_errors.incorrect: He has least money of us all.
learner_errors.correct: He has the least money of us all.
learner_errors.note: This determiner use of **least** almost always needs **the** before it.

see_also.note: **least** used before an adjective or adverb to form the superlative: *the least expensive option*

adaptation.grammar: **Least** is the superlative determiner that goes with an uncountable noun; the matching superlative for a countable noun is **fewest**, not **least**.
